key_findings.f1: Random achieved the highest Round-1 mAP@50 (0.6790), outperforming Uncertainty (0.6581) and LabelLess (0.6146) by 2.1 pp and 6.4 pp respectively.
key_findings.f2: Uncertainty achieved the highest Fire AP50 (0.6808) among all methods.
key_findings.f3: Random achieved the highest Smoke AP50 (0.7786) among all methods.
key_findings.f4: Uncertainty and Uncertainty+Rarity selected the same 100-image set in this pool. Their metrics are therefore identical (mAP50=0.6581). The rarity component did not shift the top-100 cut because the pool's score distribution places all high-uncertainty images in a near-uniform plateau.
key_findings.f5: LabelLess selected the same 100-image set as Uncertainty in both the original run (due to a stale ranked_queue.json) and after the code fix (due to data degeneracy). The top 122 pool images all have uncertainty_score=1.0, rare_class_score=0.0, and diversity_score=0.5, so adding R and D to the formula does not change which 100 images are chosen at budget=100.
key_findings.f6: This Round-1 experiment does NOT demonstrate a selection difference between Uncertainty and the full LabelLess scoring formula at budget=100 for this pool and checkpoint combination.
key_findings.f7: No claim is made about LabelLess performance in general. The observed LabelLess mAP50 difference (−0.044 vs Uncertainty) reflects differences in training data composition (human labels vs synthetic labels from ground truth), not a selection-set difference.

integrity_caveat.issue_identified: The original select_labelless() function read a static inputs/ranked_queue.json of unknown provenance instead of freshly scoring outputs/predictions.json with the canonical tri-factor formula.
integrity_caveat.fix_applied: select_labelless() in scripts/run_experiment.py was rewritten to call rank_predictions() directly from outputs/predictions.json with weights w_unc=0.70, w_rare=0.20, w_div=0.10 from config.yaml. The call site was updated from ranked_queue_path to predictions_path.
integrity_caveat.rerun_decision: The corrected LabelLess selector independently produces the same top-100 image set as the original run. This was verified by a read-only selection test showing 100/100 overlap between corrected labelless and uncertainty selections. Because the selection is identical regardless of the fix, rerunning training would produce a result that cannot be attributed to a distinct selection strategy. Training was not rerun.
integrity_caveat.data_degeneracy_explanation: 122 images in the pool have uncertainty_score=1.0 (zero detections by the base checkpoint). All 122 also have rare_class_score=0.0 and diversity_score=0.5 (zero-detection bucket). The 100-image budget fits entirely within this plateau. Adding R and D to the composite score changes the absolute priority values but not the rank order of these 122 images relative to each other, so the top-100 cut is identical under any weighting of U, R, and D.
integrity_caveat.original_result_preserved: results/metrics/round_1_labelless.json was not modified. It remains a valid trained result reflecting the original (stale-queue) run, but its selection set is not distinct from Uncertainty.
